about_sub: What is Donor.az and why was it built?
about_mission_text: Donor.az is an independent digital platform connecting blood donors with patients in need across Azerbaijan. Our goal is to simplify the blood search process and help find the right donor without wasting time.
about_what_1: Donor registration — with blood type, city and contact details
about_what_2: Urgent blood need announcements — by hospital and blood type
about_what_4: Direct contact — via call and WhatsApp
about_free_desc: Registration, search and contact — entirely at no cost.
about_safe_desc: Encrypted data storage and secure login.
about_disclaimer: Donor.az is an independent public platform. It does not provide medical advice. For any health issue, consult a doctor.
faq_sub: The most common questions about blood donation.
faq_a1: Anyone between 18-65 years old, weighing more than 50 kg, without chronic illness can donate. You should be well-rested and have eaten before donating.
faq_q2: How often can I donate blood?
faq_a2: Whole blood can be donated once every 8 weeks (56 days). Platelet donation is possible every 2 weeks.
faq_a3: Most people feel only a small pinch when the needle is inserted. The process takes 8-10 minutes and is generally painless.
faq_q4: What should I do after donating?
faq_a4: Drink plenty of water for 24 hours, avoid heavy physical work, and avoid alcohol. Eat red meat, beans and green vegetables to replenish iron stores.
faq_q5: Which blood type is most needed?
faq_a5: O− is the universal donor — it can be given to anyone. O+ is compatible with the largest portion of the population. However, all blood types are in demand.
faq_q6: I take medication — can I donate?
faq_a6: Some medications may prevent donation. If you regularly take medication, consult a doctor before donating.
faq_q7: Will I feel weak after donating?
faq_a7: Some people feel slightly dizzy after donation. To minimize this, eat well beforehand and make sure to drink fluids afterwards.
faq_q8: Why do I need to register on Donor.az?
faq_a8: Registration makes your blood type and city visible in the system. When a need arises, hospitals and family members can find you.
